key_insight: A stacked machine-learning approach and an artificial neural network were used to predict early Alzheimer’s disease from clinical, cognitive, and imaging-related data, while also highlighting likely biomarker features.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this kind of model could support earlier identification of Alzheimer’s disease stages and help clinicians prioritize patients for further assessment.
method: Used ADNI data with iterative imputation to handle missing values
Balanced classes with Borderline SVM-SMOTE and selected important features using wrapper and embedded methods
Trained a stacking ensemble (Logistic Regression, Extra Trees, Bagging KNN, LightGBM) and compared it with an ANN
evidence_signal: Model performance was evaluated with precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC on selected train/test splits from the ADNI dataset.
watch_item: Results depend on the quality and representativeness of the ADNI data, so external validation is needed before real-world use.
paper_title: Predicting Early Stages Of Alzheimer's Disease And Identifying Key Biomarkers Using Deep Artificial Neural Network And Ensemble Of Machine Learning Methodologies
